language.script_notes: Latin script with the same diacritic letters; Italian appears in some place names and signs near the northern peninsula, where an Italian-speaking minority lives.

road_furniture.guardrail_type: Heavy use along the winding coastal highway.
road_furniture.curb_style: Narrow stone-paved lanes in old towns.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Ferry terminal signs appear on the coast for the many islands.

architecture.roof_style: Low-pitched roofs covered in red terracotta tile that overlook the sea.
architecture.wall_construction: Light-coloured local limestone houses with coloured shutters and paved inner courtyards; Venetian-era stonework and loggias in walled towns; Istrian stone farmhouses in hilltop villages that recall Tuscany; a vaulted stone cellar (konoba) below many houses.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Pale gold and white stone, with green, blue or brown shutters.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Walled seaside towns; Venetian bell towers and loggias; stone villages on hilltops; drystone field walls and terraces; ferry ports and harbour front promenades.

nature.vegetation: Olive groves and vineyards, pines, cypress and low Mediterranean scrub; bare, rocky karst hillsides on the islands with drystone walls dividing small plots.
nature.terrain: A rugged limestone karst coast backed by the Dinaric mountains, with more than a thousand islands, coves and clear turquoise water.
nature.climate_signature: Hot, dry, sun-bleached Mediterranean summers and mild wet winters — bright light and a blue sea on the horizon.

vehicles.plate_color: Coastal city codes such as ST (Split), ZD (Zadar), RI (Rijeka) and DU (Dubrovnik).
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: A big seasonal presence of rental cars and foreign-plated tourist vehicles; scooters in coastal towns.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: Very dense along the coast and on the larger islands; some smaller islands have thinner coverage.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Stone architecture with terracotta roofs, especially on the northern peninsula, and Mediterranean vegetation
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The Italian bollard's diagonal red-and-black front and 'Via' street signs are absent; here the blue signs, centered red-rectangle bollard and checkerboard shield show up.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Continuation of the same karst coast and stone villages to the south
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Montenegro's plates, bollards and mixed scripts differ; the checkerboard symbol and blue signs point to this side.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same national road furniture
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The coast has red tile roofs, olive groves and karst rock; the interior is flat farmland or forested hills with Habsburg-era buildings.
